newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta shares end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta shares end slightly higher.

text.p: Calcutta share prices moved in a narrow range, closing slightly higher on Friday, brokers said
The Calcutta index ended 1.08 points up at 450.48
Brokers said that despite strong technicals, stocks could not sustain recent gains due to little interest displayed by major players.

"The mood is very dull. Neither the foreign mutual funds or Indian mutual funds and retail investors are showing any interest in buying shares. They are finding debt instruments a much safer bet as they offer better yields," said Aprajit Sharma of brokers Jet Age Securities.
"Foreign funds are buying but such small volumes can hardly be termed as support to the market," he said.
Brokers said some local punters were active buyers in steel giant TISCO on expectations that the Indian finance minister might offer some tax reliefs to the steel sector.
